what_its_for: Hydroxychloroquine is used to treat autoimmune conditions like lupus (systemic lupus erythematosus) and rheumatoid arthritis. It helps reduce pain, swelling, and skin rashes caused by these conditions. It is also sometimes used to prevent or treat malaria.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, usually once or twice a day. Always take it with food or a glass of milk to help prevent an upset stomach. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to keep a steady level in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight and the condition being treated. For lupus or rheumatoid arthritis, the usual adult dose is 200 mg to 400 mg per day. For malaria prevention, it is taken once a week. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Even a small amount can be very harmful or fatal to young children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids (like Maalox or Mylanta) within 4 hours of your dose, as they can make it harder for your body to absorb this medicine. Limit alcohol, as it can increase the risk of stomach problems. Tell your doctor about all supplements and other medicines you take, since some can interact with hydroxychloroquine. Avoid prolonged sun exposure without sunscreen, as this medicine can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice any of the following: changes in your vision or blurred vision, new eye problems, muscle weakness, hearing changes or ringing in your ears, irregular or fast heartbeat, severe mood changes or thoughts of harming yourself, signs of low blood sugar (shakiness, sweating, confusion), dark urine or yellowing of the skin or eyes, or a severe skin rash. Contact your doctor if you experience ongoing nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, or if your condition does not seem to be improving.
when_it_works: This medicine does not work overnight. For conditions like lupus or rheumatoid arthritis, it may take several weeks to months (usually 1 to 6 months) before you feel the full benefit. It is important to keep taking it even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine during pregnancy. It may be used in certain situations under close medical supervision, especially for lupus. Breastfeeding: Small amounts pass into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Children: Dosing is based on weight and must be carefully monitored. Children are especially sensitive to overdose, so keep this medicine safely locked away. Older adults: Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially eye and heart-related effects. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
